company_stage: large public enterprise technology, cloud, AI, and consulting company

culture_principles.name: Public mission and customer-impact alignment
culture_principles.description: IBM fit should connect work to the company outcomes and users described in cited public sources.

culture_principles.name: Evidence-backed execution
culture_principles.description: Strong answers should show practical judgment, clear tradeoffs, ownership, and outcomes rather than generic enthusiasm.

culture_principles.name: Client success as the primary measure
culture_principles.description: Public values material puts client success first, which means technical elegance is judged by whether the client's operation actually improves.

culture_principles.name: Innovation that has to matter
culture_principles.description: Research depth is publicly paired with enterprise applicability, so answers should connect novel work to adoption rather than to novelty alone.

culture_principles.name: Trust and personal responsibility
culture_principles.description: Enterprise and regulated clients make auditability, data handling, and clear ownership part of the engineering brief.

hiring_signals.signal: Connects decisions to the users, customers, products, or markets named in public company sources.
Uses concrete examples to show ownership, learning, and measurable improvement.
Frames a technical solution in terms of the client's operating constraint and the metric that improved.
Explains how a system stays supportable in production, including monitoring, ownership, and upgrade paths.
Shows deliberate skill acquisition when the platform or tooling changed under them.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Generic admiration for the company without a concrete role, customer, product, or business mechanism.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public lens usage should stay grounded in cited source signals and role-relevant evidence.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Describing IBM only as an AI or cloud brand without distinguishing consulting, software, infrastructure, and research work.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public sources describe materially different role families with different expectations.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Claims about internal values assessments or hiring criteria presented as public fact.
anti_signals.risk_reason: The lens is built from public-safe source metadata and does not represent an official IBM standard.

interview_patterns.pattern: Use cited public source signals to test role-relevant judgment, ownership, communication, and impact.

honest_limits: This is a lightweight public-source lens and does not represent an official IBM hiring standard.
It contains source metadata and non-verbatim public-safe signals only.
Role, team, seniority, location, and hiring manager can materially change interview emphasis.
This lens requires deeper multi-source validation before being promoted to FULLY_DISTILLED.
